---
title: "Storm Ciara: a worked example"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", echo = FALSE)
library(terra)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyterra)
devtools::load_all(quiet = TRUE)

cover_file <- system.file("extdata", "uk_nuts1_cover.tif", package = "njord")
fp_file <- system.file("extdata", "ciara_footprint_uk.tif", package = "njord")
assets_file <- system.file("extdata", "uk_litpop_025deg.tif", package = "njord")
mdd_scale <- 0.8
uk <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(country = "United Kingdom",
                                  scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
```

## Hazard: the Ciara footprint

<!-- The ranks below are typed in from data-raw/uk_storm_values.csv (written
by inst/scripts/data-raw/uk_storm_values.R). They could be computed here
instead, if that CSV (about 150 kB) were added to inst/extdata by
inst/scripts/extdata/prepare_extdata.R.

By storm severity index the two storms above Ciara are tracks 926 and 927,
both January 1984 (start dates 12 and 14 January). They may be one storm
counted twice, the two tracks sharing the same gusts; if so, Ciara is second
by severity index. -->

Storm Ciara hit the UK on 9 February 2020. In the C3S windstorm
catalogue (Hodges tracking, track 1758) it is the broadest storm over the UK
of the 1,905 from 1940 to 2026: no other storm brought gusts above 25 m/s to
so much of the UK. It stands third by storm severity index, however its highest gust
over UK land, 38.4 m/s, is unremarkable. It ranks only 145th of the total of 1,905 storms.

```{r footprint, fig.cap = "Storm Ciara footprint: the maximum 10 m gust over the 72 hours of the storm (C3S windstorm reanalysis, Hodges track 1758), m/s."}
ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = rast(fp_file)) +
  geom_sf(data = uk, fill = NA, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Gust (m/s)", na.value = "transparent") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Trigger: the UK mean gust index

The trigger index $I$ is the footprint gust averaged over UK land. Each
0.25° cell $i$ that covers some UK land has weight $w_i = f_i \cos\phi_i$,
where $f_i$ is the fraction of the cell that is UK land and $\phi_i$ its
latitude; $\cos\phi_i$ is proportional to the cell's area. Then
$I = \sum_i w_i v_i / \sum_i w_i$, with $v_i$ the cell's gust. Cells with no
gust value are left out.

```{r index, echo = TRUE}
wts <- area_weights(cover_file, regions = "UK")
index <- weighted_mean_index(values(rast(fp_file), mat = FALSE), wts)
```

For Ciara the index is `r round(index, 1)` m/s over `r length(wts$idx)`
cells with UK land cover.

The payout is a linear ramp: nothing below the attachment $A$, the full
limit $L$ above the exhaustion $E$, and a straight line between them,
$P(I) = L \min(1, \max(0, (I - A)/(E - A)))$.

```{r ramp, fig.cap = "Linear ramp payout against the UK mean gust index. The attachment (22 m/s) and exhaustion (28 m/s) are illustrative; calibrating them to storm losses with `calibrate_trigger()` is still to be done. Storm Ciara's index is the dashed line."}
attachment <- 22
exhaustion <- 28
ramp <- data.frame(index = seq(15, 35, by = 0.1))
ramp$payout <- payout(ramp$index, attachment, exhaustion, limit = 1)
ggplot(ramp, aes(index, payout)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = index, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = index, y = 0.5, label = "Ciara", hjust = 1.1) +
  labs(x = "UK mean gust index (m/s)", y = "Payout / limit") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Ciara's index of `r round(index, 1)` m/s is above the exhaustion, so the
ramp pays the full limit.
